### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /datasources/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ExternalDatasourceService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9cc0a504c8fe68720d4a2f7a863871b865a297a7` — the merge of head `bdbdaae521a95b8baf08e553ac499060b3ccd2d0` into base `d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9cc0a504c8fe68720d4a2f7a863871b865a297a7 && git checkout 9cc0a504c8fe68720d4a2f7a863871b865a297a7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2 bdbdaae521a95b8baf08e553ac499060b3ccd2d0 && git checkout -B drift-repro d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2 && git merge --no-ff bdbdaae521a95b8baf08e553ac499060b3ccd2d0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d770b1505e5b172c5a0cea2c22878067da2966b2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bdbdaae521a95b8baf08e553ac499060b3ccd2d0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/27696-external-validate-unknown-name-404.md, packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/external-datasource-unknown-name.test.ts, packages/rest/src/external-datasource-validate-scope.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/external-datasource-service.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts + packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/default-datasource-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/datasource/validate.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/external/api.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/external/ValidationPanel.tsx

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial in PR body and changeset; `record-recognisers --paths` defers to that line, as its usage text says). No governed path, no published schema in the diff.
- Ruling match (card #27696, triage 6506948888): unknown name ⇒ 404 through the one `datasourceNotFoundError`, before any validation; an existing datasource with nothing federated keeps `200 { ok: true, results: [] }`. The diff does exactly that: a three-line guard at the top of `validateDatasource` (`external-datasource-service.ts:1231-1233`), byte-identical to `testConnection`'s (#27510, line 723), ahead of `listObjects()` and `validateEach`.
- Q1 (who is refused): only a name for which `config.getDatasource` resolves nothing, with `default` short-circuited. `getDatasource` is wired to `metadata.get('datasource', n)` (`service-datasource/src/plugin.ts:181`), the same read `GET /datasources/:name` makes (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:437`, `getDatasourceRecord`). Every datasource that exists has a record there: admin-created ones via `metadata.register('datasource', …)` (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:448`), code-defined / app-bundle ones via `registerInMemory('datasource', …)` (`app-plugin.ts:1335`), the primary via `DefaultDatasourcePlugin.registerVisibility` (`default-datasource-plugin.ts:288`) and, independently, the `DEFAULT_DATASOURCE_NAME` short-circuit. A bare `DriverPlugin` registers a driver service, not a datasource (`driver-plugin.ts:50-58`), so it is not a datasource the sibling doors answer either. No new false-404 source beyond what `testConnection` and GET already have.
- Q1 (who keeps 200): managed datasources (`warehouse`, no `schemaMode`) and `default` are pinned at `200 { ok: true, results: [] }` over the real service and real `HonoHttpServer` (`external-datasource-unknown-name.test.ts`); the `default` pin runs with `getDatasource` returning undefined, so it pins the short-circuit itself. Existence only, not `assertFederationSource` (which would 400 managed and primary) — correct per ruling.
- Q2 (before listing/introspection): the service pin asserts `listObjects` never called and nothing introspected; the rest scope test asserts `introspected === []` and `validateAll` not called.
- Q3 (consistency): `datasourceNotFoundError` is the single factory (`datasource-admin-service.ts:352`: status 404, code `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `Datasource "NAME" does not exist.`), used by GET/update/delete, `assertFederationSource` (#27618) and `testConnection` (#27510). The route relays it unchanged via `refused` → `answerThrown` (`external-datasource-routes.ts:479-480`), which already special-cases `{status: 404, code: RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND}`; the route diff is comment-only, consistent with the PR's claim.
- Q4 (drift check): `runDriftCheck` wraps `validateDatasource` in try/catch (`external-validation-plugin.ts:~500`): one `warn` "drift check could not be performed", `return 0`, no events, no throw; the timer is fire-and-forget (`void this.runDriftCheck`) so no unhandled rejection. The throwing path is already pinned (`external-validation-plugin.test.ts:218`). Timers are only cleared at plugin stop (lines 254-255), never on datasource delete — that is a pre-existing lifecycle gap; the PR turns a silent empty report into one warn per configured interval for a deleted datasource, which is the honest degradation the file's own doc comment prescribes. Not a crash loop.
- Q6 (clients): `packages/client` `datasources.external.validate` uses `unwrapResponse` (throws on a failing envelope); CLI `os datasource validate` reads the envelope and `this.error(envelope.message)` on `ok:false` — a 404 now reports `Datasource "x" does not exist.` instead of "No federated objects to validate." (an improvement, exit non-zero); UI `ValidationPanel` catches and shows the message in `error` state, and is only ever invoked for a datasource it is rendering (one that exists). No caller relied on the 200 for an unknown name. Sibling repos (objectui, hotcrm) hold the same UI code only.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/service-datasource`: `patch` with BREAKING banner — correct: `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ patch; a non-protocol narrowing keeps its banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task §3).
- `@objectstack/rest` publishes no code change (comment + tests), so no second changeset is owed. The behaviour change reaches REST via the dependency; the changeset body names the route explicitly.
- Before / Now / Fix carried in the changeset body; marker `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is a recognised category (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:147`) and fits: no authorable key, value or stored shape moves; CI gates at the head are green (35 success / 13 skipped, 0 failing).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tier: no governed surface, no `packages/spec` touch, no `IExternalDatasourceService` interface change (`validateDatasource` stays off the spec interface, per its doc comment).
- Declarations present and line-initial in both PR body and changeset; `Skills-docs: none` is grep-backed in the body; title carries `!`.
- File surface: wider than the dispatch order (service file + test added) — amended on the claim before push, and the dev report measured why (the route already relays; the empty report was the service's). Accepted.
- Head repo is `objectstack-ai/objectstack` (not a fork). PR is draft; landing is the seat's after this record and the seat's ACCEPT.
- Note for a follow-up card, not a must-fix: `scheduleDriftChecks` never disarms a timer when its datasource is deleted at runtime; with this PR that datasource logs one warn per interval until restart.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing takes away nothing a consumer could use: the old `200 { ok: true, results: [] }` for a nonexistent name was indistinguishable from "exists, nothing federated", and the ruling closes exactly that ambiguity. The spec's own refusal (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` for an unaddressable datasource, as every by-name door answers) is made real on the last by-name door that lacked it.
- Reusing `testConnection`'s existence check verbatim (not `assertFederationSource`) is the right narrowing: it refuses only absence, and keeps managed and primary datasources at their empty report, which is what the ruling asks and what the 200 pins hold.
- Pins are placed on both sides: service (throw shape, nothing listed/introspected) and REST (status, envelope, message in GET's words, `data` absent), plus the pre-existing scope test flipped rather than deleted, so the "dials nothing" guarantee survives the status change.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-rsztyz`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia (seat subagent)`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Seat ACCEPT · PR #27911 · head `bdbdaae521a95b8baf08e553ac499060b3ccd2d0` · 2026-10-30T03:55Z

## 维护者速读

`POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/validate` now answers a datasource name that does not exist with `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, in the same words as `GET /datasources/:name` and `testConnection`. Before, it answered `200 { ok: true, results: [] }`, which a caller could not tell apart from "exists, nothing federated". A datasource that exists keeps its `200` empty report: the primary one, managed ones, and ones with nothing bound. The runtime drift check meets the new refusal only for a datasource deleted after its timer was armed. It lands in its existing catch: one `warn`, no events.

- **Shape:** draft → main, with `Fixes #27696`. Six files: the `validateDatasource` existence check in service-datasource and its test, a comment on the rest route, two rest tests, and a changeset. `check-governed-merges --pr 27911`: NOT governed, +137 / −15.

- **Contract review:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record 6514562181 (PASS at this head). Claim 6514492084.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Consistent.
- **Skills-docs:** `none`, with the grep reason on the PR body.

  - the `HOOK_ABORTED` pins (#27806, fixed on `main` by #27878);
  - `sys_exchange_rate` entry-views (#27813 range).

- **Gate check-runs on this head:** 48 total, 35 success, 13 skipped by the path filter, 0 failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.
